name: Familial Adrenal Hypoplasia with Absent Pituitary Luteinizing Hormone
aliases: Congenital Adrenal Hypoplasia with Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism
X-linked Adrenal Hypoplasia Congenita with LH Deficiency

criteria.description: Evidence of adrenal cortex hypoplasia confirmed by imaging or histology
Biochemical evidence of absent or severely reduced pituitary luteinizing hormone secretion
Clinical and laboratory features consistent with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
Identification of pathogenic NR0B1 (DAX1) gene mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of adrenal hypoplasia, absent pituitary LH secretion, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with confirmation of NR0B1 mutation or compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for NR0B1 mutations is critical for confirmation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary adrenal insufficiency with salt-wasting crisis
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: adrenal gland failure with salt loss
low adrenal hormones causing salt crisis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or severely reduced pituitary luteinizing hormone secretion
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with delayed or absent puberty
pathognomonic.notes: Manifested by lack of secondary sexual characteristics
searchTerms: delayed puberty due to low hormones
hypogonadism with late or no puberty

common.symptomName: Hyperpigmentation of skin and mucous membranes
searchTerms: darkening of skin and mucous membranes
need for salty foods with dehydration

common.notes: Secondary to electrolyte imbalance and cortisol deficiency

common.symptomName: Cryptorchidism or micropenis in affected males

searchTerms: low blood sugar episodes in babies

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting during adrenal crises
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting during adrenal crisis

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias related to electrolyte disturbances

rare.notes: Due to chronic cortisol replacement therapy
Reported in some adolescent or adult patients

laboratory: Low serum cortisol with elevated ACTH
Low serum luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone
Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and hypoglycemia during adrenal crisis
imaging: Small or hypoplastic adrenal glands on abdominal ultrasound or MRI
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in NR0B1 (DAX1) gene on X chromosome
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Enzyme deficiencies causing adrenal hyperplasia rather than hypoplasia
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia or hyposmia
No adrenal insufficiency or salt-wasting crises

redFlags: Salt-wasting crisis with dehydration and hypotension in infancy
Delayed or absent puberty with hypogonadism
Family history of early male infant deaths or adrenal insufficiency
references: Achermann JC, et al. NR0B1 mutations and adrenal hypoplasia congenita. Trends Endocrinol Metab. 2020.
Orphanet: Familial adrenal hypoplasia with absent pituitary luteinizing hormone (ORPHA:95700)
Speiser PW, et al. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to steroid 21-hydroxylase deficiency: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2018.
